title: Minimum Description Length Monitor: Compression-Based Anomaly Detection for AI Agent Behavior
original_idea: Represent agent trajectories as strings over action type vocabulary. Compute compression ratio using gzip/zstd. Establish baseline from 100 benign METR traces. Flag SHADE-Arena trajectories outside baseline distribution. Evaluate AUC and compare to isolation forest.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory: compression captures structural regularity, and malicious trajectories may have unusual structure. But the connection between compression ratio and safety-relevant behavior is indirect and may not hold if malicious actions are structurally similar to benign ones.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Trivially simple implementation: import gzip, compress strings, compare ratios. No ML needed for the main approach. Isolation forest comparison is one scikit-learn call. Very accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Extremely narrow: compress trajectories, compute ratios, compare distributions, report AUC. Single clear experiment with a single deliverable metric.
